result.topic_en: Euler combines gravity, pressure gradient and frictional retardation into a differential equation for the water pressure p along the tube, integrates it with the factor e^{αr}, and expands the solution in a series in the small friction coefficient α.
result.transcription:
DE FRICTIONE FLVIDORVM. 345
naſcetur hinc vis acceleratrix ſecundum directionem
M$m$ directa $= -\frac{dp}{ds}$, exiſtente $p$ functione ipſius $s$, ſeu
ipſarum $x$ et $y$.
21. Tertio ob frictionem motui aquae reſiſti-
tur vi retardatrice $= \frac{\alpha p}{z}$, vti ſupra §. 11. eſt oſten-
ſum, vnde vis acceleratrix aquae ſecundum directionem
M$m$ erit $= -\frac{\alpha p}{z}$. Cum igitur aqua his tribus viribus
ſubiiciatur, neceſſe eſt, vt ſit:
$-\frac{4b^4 v dz}{z^5 ds} = \cos.\Phi - \frac{dp}{ds} - \frac{\alpha p}{z}$,
ſeu $dx - dp - \frac{\alpha p ds}{z} + \frac{4b^4 v dz}{z^5} = 0$ ob $ds\cos.\Phi = dx$.
22. Peruenimus ergo ad hanc aequationem,
ex qua primo $p$ ſtatus compreſſionis aquae in loco quocun-
que tubi MN definiri debet,
$dp + \frac{\alpha p ds}{z} = dx + \frac{4b^4 v dz}{z^5}$
quae multiplicata per $e^{\alpha\int\frac{ds}{z}}$ denotante $e$ numerum cu-
ius logarithmus hyperbolicus eſt $= 1$, fit integrabilis.
Habebitur enim poſito breuitatis gratia $\int\frac{ds}{z} = r$:
$e^{\alpha r} p = C + \int e^{\alpha r} dx + 4b^4 v \int \frac{e^{\alpha r} dz}{z^5}$.
23. Valor autem huius integralis $\int\frac{ds}{z} = r$ ita
ſit acceptus, vt in ſupremo vaſis loco AB, ſeu vbi
$x = 0$, euaneſcat. Quo poſito, cum $\alpha$ ſit fractio ve-
hementer parua,
erit $e^{\alpha r} = 1 + \alpha r + \frac{1}{2}\alpha^2 r^2 + \frac{1}{6}\alpha^3 r^3 + \frac{1}{24}\alpha^4 r^4 + \text{etc.}$
erit $e^{\alpha r} p = C + x + \alpha\int r\,dx + \frac{1}{2}\alpha^2\int rr\,dx + \frac{1}{6}\alpha^3\int r^3 dx$
$-\frac{b^4 v}{z^4} - 4\alpha b^4 v\int\frac{r\,dz}{z^5} - 2\alpha^2 b^4 v\int\frac{rr\,dz}{z^5} - \frac{2}{3}\alpha^3 b^4 v\int\frac{r^3 dz}{z^5} - \text{etc.}$
24. Cum ſit $dr = \frac{ds}{z}$, integratio etiam hoc
modo inſtitui poteſt:
Tom. VI. Nou. Com. X x $\int e^{\alpha r}$
